newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq newspapers assail U.S. for "silly stories".
newsitem.headline: Iraq newspapers assail U.S. for "silly stories".

text.p: Iraq's official press on Friday joined the government in attacking U.S. allegations of a power struggle in Baghdad.
Al-Iraq newspaper, in a front-page editorial, said U.S. officials knew they were not telling the truth but were trying ..."to create flagrant lies and shroud them with false credibility."
"We advise the American administration to ...stop the unleashing of such silly stories and prevent itself from turning into a laughing stock," the paper said.
"Things like this have no grain of truth but in their dark and sick dreams," declared al-Thawra, organ of the ruling Baath party.

The two newspapers lambasted Samuel Berger, U.S. national security adviser; Mike McCurry, the White House spokesman; Defence Secretary William Cohen and Nicholas Burns, State Department spokesman, who they said exchanged roles in making silly remarks about Iraq.
"They are a batch of liars," said al- Iraq.

In Washington on Wednesday, McCurry, following suggestions of instability in Iraq reported on Tuesday by a senior U.S. military official, said:"There are a great deal of complicated internal struggles for power" going on.

The senior U.S. military official said that President Saddam Hussein had put his wife under house arrest and was changing locations more often out of apparent fear for his safety, and that his son Uday, who was shot and wounded in Baghdad on December 12, might lose a leg to gangrene.
Al-Iraq likened latest statements by U.S. officials to "science fiction films which Hollywood churns out."
The papers also carried remarks by Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf in which he described the allegations as "a silly comic play."
